facts.material: electric motor (stator, rotor, housing, drive electronics)
facts.function: converts DC electrical energy to rotary motion (spins the scanning element)
facts.form: DC brushless motor assembly, a subcomponent

gri_path: Section XVI note 2(a): a part that is itself a good of a chapter 85 heading (8501 motors) is classified in that heading, not as a part of the scanner (8471/8473)
GRI 6: 8501.10 output not exceeding 37.5 W (assumed, small scanner motor); of under 18.65 W; not synchronous valued under $4 so 8501.10.40; DC, brushless suffix .40

rejected_alternatives.reason: Section XVI note 2(a): a motor of heading 8501 stays in its own heading even when dedicated to a scanner
applies to motors of 18.65 W or more; bar code scanner motors are typically only a few watts
DC motors over 37.5 W; output far lower

missing_facts: What is the rated output in watts (assumed under 18.65 W)?
Does the assembly include a polygon mirror or other optical element that could change its character?
classification.rationale: A DC brushless motor is named by heading 8501, and Section XVI note 2(a) keeps such a good in its own heading even when it is a subcomponent of a laser scanner. Small scanner motors have an output well under 18.65 W, placing it in 8501.10.40, DC brushless. NY H87929 (in force) classified a small DC brushless motor in the same line, 8501.10.4040.
